title: Chennai Love Story Crosses ₹24 Crore Worldwide in Opening Weekend, Surpasses SK Kalyana Mandapam
excerpt: Kiran Abbavaram's Telugu romantic drama defied a crowded release window to collect ₹7.48 crore on Day 3, now his third-highest-grossing film and closing in on the ₹26.94 crore record set by KA.
body:
• Chennai Love Story earned ₹7.48 crore on Day 3 (Sunday), bringing its worldwide gross to ₹24.78 crore in three days — surpassing the lifetime collection of Kiran Abbavaram's SK Kalyana Mandapam (₹11.31 crore).
  • The film's India net stands at ₹17.20 crore after three days, recovering over 50% of its ₹30 crore production budget.
  • Strong occupancy rates in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — particularly Hyderabad (68.5%), Vizag (79%), and Guntur (82.3%) on Sunday — drove the weekend surge.
  • The film now chases Abbavaram's career-best KA (₹26.94 crore net), which it could surpass within the first week.

Defying the Competition

Chennai Love Story opened on July 24 in a release window dominated by Thalapathy Vijay's Jana Nayagan, a film most competitors chose to avoid entirely. The decision to hold the date has paid off.

The Telugu romantic drama, directed by Ravi Namburi and starring Kiran Abbavaram and Sri Gauri Priya, collected ₹5.69 crore on its opening Friday, rose to ₹6.61 crore on Saturday, and pushed further to ₹7.48 crore on Sunday, according to data from Sacnilk. The upward trajectory across all three days — unusual for a mid-budget Telugu film — points to strong word-of-mouth driving audiences into theaters.

After three days, the India net collection stands at ₹17.20 crore, with a gross of ₹19.78 crore. Overseas markets added ₹5.00 crore gross, taking the worldwide total to ₹24.78 crore.

The Numbers That Matter

The weekend performance places Chennai Love Story comfortably ahead of Abbavaram's 2022 hit SK Kalyana Mandapam, which finished its entire theatrical run at ₹11.31 crore net. The film surpassed that total by the end of Day 2 itself.

It is now Abbavaram's third-highest-grossing film, and based on current momentum, appears likely to overtake KA (2024), which holds his personal record at ₹26.94 crore net. Given that Monday typically sees a drop for Telugu releases, the Day 4 collection of ₹3.42 crore represents a healthy hold.

Produced on a budget of ₹30 crore by Srinivasa Kumar and Sai Rajesh under Mass Movie Makers and Amrutha Productions, the film has already recovered over 57% of its cost through India net collections alone. Reaching break-even looks increasingly realistic by the end of its first week.

"Chennai Love Story outperformed Jana Nayagan at several locations across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana over the weekend, an achievement few predicted."

— Zoom TV Entertainment

Regional Dominance

The bulk of the film's revenue comes from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, which accounted for ₹20.40 crore of the ₹23.20 crore four-day India gross. Karnataka contributed ₹2.37 crore, while the rest of India and Kerala made up the remainder.

Sunday occupancy figures tell the story of a film that has connected deeply with its target audience. Guntur led with 82.3% overall occupancy, followed by Vizag-Visakhapatnam at 79%, Hyderabad at 68.5%, and Warangal at 68.8%. Chennai, with just eight shows, hit a near-perfect 99% occupancy.

The regional concentration is typical for a Telugu romantic drama without major pan-India ambitions, but the numbers within that core market are exceptional for a film at this budget level.

What Made It Work

Chennai Love Story explores first love between two young people navigating the emotional intensity that comes with it. Despite mixed initial reviews from critics, audiences — particularly younger demographics in the AP-Telangana belt — have responded to the combination of Abbavaram's growing star power and Mani Sharma's music, which has generated significant buzz on social media.

The film also benefited from a relatively clear lane. While Jana Nayagan dominated screens nationwide, it left enough room in Telugu-heavy markets for Chennai Love Story to find its audience without head-to-head competition for shows.

The Road to ₹30 Crore

The critical question is whether the film can sustain its run through the weekdays. Monday's ₹3.42 crore drop of roughly 54% from Sunday is standard for the market. If it holds at ₹2-3 crore daily through the week, it could clear its budget by next weekend.

For Abbavaram, 26, the stakes go beyond this single film. A budget-crossing performance would cement his position as one of Telugu cinema's most reliable mid-range draws, following up on KA's success two years ago with a film that has shown even stronger opening momentum.
